newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals weaker in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals weaker in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended a quiet day mostly lower on Thursday, pressured by the yen's firmer tone against the dollar and weaker precious metal prices in New York on Wednesday, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from two to seven yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was five yen lower at 1,340 yen.

Gold premiums in the spot Tokyo gold market were quoted at about 10 U.S. cents above the dollar-based spot gold price on a C and F basis, recovered from about 50 cents below the spot gold on Monday, but down from about 40 to 50 cent premiums earlier last week.

"Reflecting the South Korean government's crackdown on speculative gold trade, gold flows from South Korea into the Tokyo spot market have declined. But Japanese gold premiums are still at lows due to weak gold demand and gold flows from South Africa," a trading house trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $385.90/386.40 per ounce at 0800 GMT, against $385.50/386.00 in New York on Wednesday.
Some traders said spot gold may test the support of $395 as market sentiment was dampened by a lack of reaction from the Iraq-U.S. tensions.
The Tokyo precious metal market was focused on Friday's U.S. employment data for signs of inflation, and its likely effect on the market.
Platinum prices fell in line with lower spot platinum prices amid a dearth of fresh incentives.
Platinum prices ranged from six to 12 yen per gram weaker. Benchmark August was 12 yen lower at 1,367 yen.
Silver prices ranged from unchanged to 1.1 yen per 10 grams lower. Benchmark August stood 1.1 yen weaker at 182.9 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from two yen per gram lower to one yen firmer. Benchmark August was 1.0 yen lower at 439 yen.
